prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1262; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is for claim purposes. Do you understand and agree to being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Can you tell me, in your own words, what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was driving home on a two-lane road in League City, going maybe thirty miles an hour. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane while taking a curve, and we ended up hitting head-on. It wasn't a violent crash, but it was enough to jolt me forward and then back.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy in your vehicle?

A: No, they didn't. I just felt the seatbelt tighten across my chest and shoulder.

Q: Did you get out of the car or go to a doctor right away?

A: I got out and stood by the road for a bit. My right shoulder was sore, but I figured it would pass. The other driver seemed okay, and we exchanged information. A couple of days later the pain got worse, so I went to urgent care.

Q: What injuries were you diagnosed with?

A: They said it was a strain in my right shoulder. The doctor recommended rest, some physical therapy, and an anti-inflammatory. I still have trouble lifting my arm above my head and sleeping on that side.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: I've missed a few shifts. I'm waiting on my employer to send paperwork for that.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?

A: Only that I've been keeping my physical therapy appointments and I want to get back to normal as soon as I can.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
